target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2023 disclosure outlines the IDM 2.0 strategy combining internal factories, foundry capacity, and an Open System Foundry. The 2024 disclosure D015 specifically details the 'Foundry services' component of this strategy, describing the expansion of foundry business for external customers, the high capital requirements, and the differentiation through technology and capacity. This is the direct continuation of the IDM 2.0 foundry expansion topic.

Both disclosures describe the expansion of Intel's foundry business for external customers, characterized by the same four components: wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplets (or chiplet standard), and software (or software/services). 2023 D019 mentions 'Open System Foundry... four components: wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplet standard, and software'. 2024 D015 mentions 'foundry offerings include four components: wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplets, and software and services'. Both also mention differentiation through leading-edge technology/packaging and committed capacity/IP.

current_disclosures.summary: Intel is transitioning its semiconductor manufacturing business from an internal-product-focused model to a customer-centric foundry business to improve financial viability amid rising costs, while also aiming to participate in the demand for U.S.-based foundry capacity. comparisons.peer_summary: Many major customer relationships are long-standing and result from years of collaborative product development, which has enabled Broadcom to build an extensive IP portfolio and gain critical system-level knowledge. This collaboration provides key insights into customer businesses, enhancing efficiency and the ability to serve target markets.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both highlight the value of deep customer collaboration in building their respective IP portfolios and understanding market needs, though Intel frames this in the context of an emerging foundry business serving external customers while Broadcom cites it as a result of long-standing relationships for existing products. Intel states, "we are seeking to build a world-class foundry business also serving external customers and have made significant investments in ecosystem support" (intc_2024_1_P014_S003). Broadcom describes its advantage as stemming from "years of collaborative product development" that enabled it to "build our extensive IP portfolio and develop critical expertise regarding our customers' requirements" (avgo_2024_1_P033_S007, avgo_2024_1_P033_S008).

sentences.text: To this end, we are seeking to build a world-class foundry business also serving external customers and have made significant investments in ecosystem support to enable the usage of our manufacturing network by external customers.
Many of our major customer relationships have been in place for many years and are often the result of years of collaborative product development.
This has enabled us to build our extensive IP portfolio and develop critical expertise regarding our customers' requirements, including substantial system-level knowledge.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company sells and licenses its technology to third parties to monetize intellectual property investments, including through joint developments, though it cannot predict if future licenses will be obtained or renewed on acceptable terms.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron discuss monetizing and licensing their intellectual property, including joint developments with third parties, as part of their broader business strategies. Intel's foundry offering includes "software and services" (intc_2024_1_P014_S004) and its strategy involves "ecosystem support to enable the usage of our manufacturing network by external customers" (intc_2024_1_P014_S003). Micron explicitly states, "we sell and/or license our technology to other parties and continue to pursue opportunities to monetize our investments in our intellectual property through partnering and other arrangements" and notes it has "jointly developed memory and storage product and process technology with third parties" (mu_2024_1_P066_S001, mu_2024_1_P066_S002).

sentences.text: Our foundry offerings include four components: wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplets, and software and services.

To this end, we are seeking to build a world-class foundry business also serving external customers and have made significant investments in ecosystem support to enable the usage of our manufacturing network by external customers.

From time to time, we sell and/or license our technology to other parties and continue to pursue opportunities to monetize our investments in our intellectual property through partnering and other arrangements.
We have also jointly developed memory and storage product and process technology with third parties on a limited basis.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and cost benefits
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA utilizes a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, employing partners for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging to avoid significant costs and risks associated with owning manufacturing operations. This approach allows the company to focus resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support.
comparisons.comparison: Intel discloses a strategic shift to expand its internal manufacturing capabilities into an external foundry business to utilize high capital investments in leading-edge nodes like Intel 18A, whereas NVIDIA explicitly employs a fabless strategy to avoid the significant costs and risks associated with owning manufacturing operations. Intel states, "The very high capital requirements of modern leading-edge semiconductor process technology... require us to expand the use of our process technologies... and grow the number of wafers produced beyond the expected growth for our own products" (intc_2024_1_P014_S002), while NVIDIA notes, "We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy... we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations" (nvda_2024_1_P043_S001).

sentences.text: The very high capital requirements of modern leading-edge semiconductor process technology development and manufacturing, especially those nodes requiring EUV lithography such as Intel 4, Intel 3, Intel 18A and future nodes, require us to expand the use of our process technologies as they mature and grow the number of wafers produced beyond the expected growth for our own products.

To this end, we are seeking to build a world-class foundry business also serving external customers and have made significant investments in ecosystem support to enable the usage of our manufacturing network by external customers.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA leverages its intellectual property as a valuable asset, accessing it to customers and partners through license and development agreements to enhance technology reach.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies leverage intellectual property as a strategic asset through licensing, though Intel's IP strategy is specifically tied to its foundry differentiation by including x86 cores in its IP portfolio, while NVIDIA focuses on broader technology access for custom development. Intel plans to differentiate its foundry offerings through "a world-class IP portfolio that will include x86 cores" (intc_2024_1_P014_S006). Similarly, NVIDIA states, "We believe our IP is a valuable asset that can be accessed by our customers and partners through license and development agreements when they desire to build such capabilities directly into their own products" (nvda_2024_1_P038_S002).

sentences.text: We plan to differentiate our foundry offerings from those of others through a combination of leading-edge packaging and process technology, committed capacity in the US and Europe available for customers globally, and a world-class IP portfolio that will include x86 cores, as well as other ecosystem IP.

We believe our IP is a valuable asset that can be accessed by our customers and partners through license and development agreements when they desire to build such capabilities directly into their own products or have us do so through a custom development.
